iut_type: Panasonic wireless lighting control product (nRF52, SoftDevice S113)
customer_question: The product will use SoftDevice S113 instead of S140. S140 is already registered. Does adding S113 require additional RF PHY testing?
question_variants: S113 added to product with existing S140 registration — is additional RF test needed?
Does switching from S140 to S113 SoftDevice require new RF certification?
S140 covers S113 functionality — does S113 require its own RF PHY test?
actual_issue: The existing product (nRF52 with SoftDevice S140 6.1.x) is registered. A new model variant will use SoftDevice S113. The customer wonders if S113 requires a separate RF PHY test.
plain_english_explanation: Nordic Semiconductor's SoftDevice S140 implements all the Bluetooth features of both S140 and S113 — S140 is a superset of S113. Because S140 fully includes all S113 functionality (Host and Link Layer), any product that uses S113 can be added to the existing registration as a derivative product, inheriting the S140 test results. No additional RF PHY test is required when adding S113-based variants to an existing S140 registration.
consultant_answer: S140 includes (is a superset of) S113 functionality. Therefore, adding an S113-based product variant to the existing S140 registration does not require additional RF PHY testing. The S113 variant can be added as a derivative model to the existing registration's Product List at no additional RF test cost.
decision_logic: When a Host/LL SoftDevice version is a subset of an already-registered version (S113 ⊂ S140), the existing RF PHY test coverage applies to the subset version. No new RF test is needed. This is a general principle: if the new variant uses a less capable version of an already-tested stack, the existing test results remain valid.
final_recommendation: Add the S113-based model as a derivative product to the existing S140 registration's Product List. No additional RF PHY test is required. The registration for the new model with S113 can proceed as a free derivative product addition.
risk_if_done_wrong: Unnecessarily requiring a new RF PHY test for S113 when S140 is already registered adds cost and delay to a registration that could proceed as a free derivative addition.
